wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.

admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by capability actions. The authorizing actions are exactly the ones whose target_event_kinds list this kind in capability-action-registry; there is no second per-event list. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a PCR ak.realm.create with no did_inception ref and with both executed_by and authorization_ref. A purpose=agent_control Agent branch MUST carry exactly one critical refs[] role=agent_provision pointing to the accepted controller-authored ak.agent.provision Event; the verifier cross-binds actor_id, realm_id, controller, PCR delegation and provision payload before the reducer materializes the Agent active status cell. An explicitly organization-governed purpose=principal_control branch MUST carry zero agent_provision refs and MUST prove its separate accepted organization authority. The two branches are disjoint; a self-principal or generic realm.create capability substitution is rejected. This class never authorizes a following device-authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.applet_managed_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for purpose=applet_managed_control ak.realm.create carrying exactly one critical refs[] role=applet_managed_actor_provision. The referenced accepted ak.applet.managed_actor.provision is immutable and cross-binds the exact account ActorId, applet/service/registration/authority, role, event-derived realm_id and object.initial_resolution. executed_by MUST equal the provision service_id and authorization_ref MUST equal its applet_authority_ref. It never substitutes Agent or human PCR admission.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.registration_anchor: Admitted only for self-principal PCR genesis using durable registration-time DID control evidence and one critical did_inception ref. The verifier validates the accepted-at adapter/method evidence and project(did)=actor_id; current DID state after registration is irrelevant.
admission_class_definitions.pcr_recovery: Admitted only for ak.device.reanchor under the account-local lineage's accepted PCR recovery policy/session and monotonic generation CAS. did_root is merely one optional policy-enabled factor. A current DID proof without the matching account-local lineage and policy cannot enter this class.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_agent_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_agent_provision pointing to an accepted ak.agent.provision Event. Used solely for the controller-to-own-Agent Direct Conversation branch, which has no Contact round. The verifier cross-binds participants to exactly that controller and Agent, requires the Direct Conversation profile rather than a PCR profile, checks the controller binding is current, and fixes founder = controller so the Agent runtime key never needs Direct Conversation founding scope. This role is structurally exclusive with direct_conversation_contact_round and with the Agent PCR agent_provision role.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_contact_round pointing to the portable Contact round evidence bundle and its continuity chain to the pair's root Contact round. The verifier derives founder from the root Contact round (normal branch: the sorted_pair_member_ids entry that is not the request_event_ref issuer_id, i.e. the responder; glare branch: the requests[0] issuer_id), then requires created_by == actor_id == founder, recomputes pair_key from sorted_pair_member_ids and the trust domain, and pins the Direct Conversation profile, exact-two participants and the create-locked encryption and history baseline. Accepted-at Contact round validity and current directional Contact gates are evaluated separately so Event validity never depends on delivery order.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Every standard ak.* Event.kind admitted through Event Envelope MUST appear in this registry. Signal payload types and DeviceMessageEnvelope message kinds are intentionally outside this Event registry.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.

Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into shared Realm data-plane history or control-plane Seal history.

lifecycle_modality applies to physical object lifecycle writes, identified mechanically by an fsm_contract whose axis is object_lifecycle, plus explicitly registered reversible Realm lifecycle facets. Every active event kind that writes such a family MUST declare lifecycle_modality. Use reversible for a reversible facet or either member of an archive/restore pair, and terminal for an irreversible transition. Workflow, membership, status, audit, key-material and OR-Set revocation axes are excluded. Reducers and SDKs MUST read this field and MUST NOT infer modality from event-kind spelling.

Every active reducer-input durable kind MUST declare plane, sealed, and a complete machine-readable cell_writes[] contract; no parallel single-target fields or aliases exist. Each entry declares cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, optional initial_value, and optional condition. A condition marks the target as conditional. Payload conditions use the closed grammar field_present|field_absent|field_equals|any_field_present; a signed semantic-ref condition uses only critical_ref_role_exact_count{role,count}. All are pure functions of the schema-validated signed Event. When the condition holds the target is required and the reducer MUST derive exactly one matching write from kind+payload; when it does not hold the reducer MUST NOT derive that write. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2. cell_family is a stable ak.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, an explicitly sourced payload.* or envelope.actor_id field path, a canonical_json descriptor for a closed structured identifier (key bytes are its RFC 8785 JCS bytes), a coalesce descriptor, or a composite descriptor whose structured components use the same canonical_json descriptor. Bare field paths and other envelope.* fields are invalid. plane MUST be data or control; sealed is a boolean and MUST be true iff plane=control. plane/sealed are the machine-readable authority for DataEvent versus Control Move routing and plane_cross_write validation; payload prose is explanatory. bottom is reject, expose, or inert; inert MUST be used when the lattice cannot produce Bottom. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any reducer write has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` implements singleton-once-set cells.

The ak.component.agent.status.v1 lifecycle cell is keyed only by the complete Agent account ActorId: agent-control ak.realm.create and every ak.self.agent.pause, ak.self.agent.resume, or ak.self.agent.deactivate write MUST use the identical single-component composite canonical_json(envelope.actor_id) subject. The Agent actor MUST be the account variant; a service actor is invalid. payload.agent_id is a redundant principal cross-binding and MUST equal envelope.actor_id.account_id.principal_id, but it never addresses the cell. payload.controller_id MUST equal executed_by.account_id.principal_id. Missing or unequal bindings fail closed, and Account ActorIds with the same principal_id at different station_id values MUST derive different subjects.

Every lattice=fsm cell write MUST resolve by cell_family to exactly one fsm_contract. Event-kind parameters MUST NOT duplicate states or allowed_transitions. Template-backed contracts resolve their instance_parameters before transition validation; unresolved templates, parameters or conditional edges fail closed.

Every active wire_scope=actor_private_event kind MUST resolve to exactly one entry in actor_private_contracts.event_writes. Actor-private writes use only the registered actor_private_contracts.cell_families merge contract, never shared Realm plane/sealed routing, CBA fields, reducer_input, or shared cell_contracts.

Protocol-singleton cells MAY take their genesis value from a create payload, but every subsequent write MUST use a registered event_kind. ak.component.notary.v1 and ak.component.realm.reducer_profile.v1 are canonically defined in zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md; their genesis values come from ak.realm.create, and subsequent writes use ak.realm.notary and ak.realm.upgrade respectively.

Lattice MUST be one of the fully specified core types: or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log. A new lattice type cannot become active until its join, bottom, op schema, profile gate, and conformance vectors are all registered.

Every ordered_log append MUST project issuer_seq from envelope.actor_seq exactly. The coordinate is sparse within a cell; join retains every accepted Event sibling and digest order is serialization-only. A registry row MUST NOT declare a cell-local constant or payload counter, slot winner, prefix gap, or authorization effect for ordered_log.

State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvent writes are projected and locally accepted against seal_ref, Control Move writes are projected and finalized by Seals, and per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic. Event Envelope routing fields MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

Every active durable reducer-input event_kind MUST have a machine-readable admission source: either at least one capability action targets it (capability_action_registry.target_event_kinds), or it declares an admission class from admission_class_definitions. capability_gated events MUST be listed in at least one action's target_event_kinds - admission has a single direction of truth and no per-event capability list. Enforced by tools/artifact_lint; no active durable reducer-input event may lack an admission source (fail-closed).

A conditional admission MUST use only selectors defined by admission_predicate_contract. All non-otherwise predicates are evaluated independently; exactly one match selects its branch, zero matches selects the final otherwise branch, and multiple matches fail closed. otherwise is never evaluated as an ordinary predicate.

ak.conflict.recovery is the single registered exception to literal cell addressing. Its one cell_writes[] entry declares cell_ref (a cell_id sourced from the payload) instead of cell_family/cell_subject, and effect_projection kind=reset instead of a lattice op, and it omits lattice and bottom. That combination is closed: no other kind may declare cell_ref or reset, and this kind MUST declare both together. A recovery addresses one cell of an arbitrary family, so the target cannot be a literal ak.component.*.v<n> URI; and a reset is not a join, so it has no lattice. The safety envelope is not static reachability but zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.5: the reducer MUST apply a reset only to a cell already in Bottom, and only when the Event carries refs[] role=recovery_capability and role=state_witness satisfying every condition in that section. On a cell in any other state the write MUST be rejected.

Every active standard Event kind MUST declare exactly one payload_schema_ref. The reference MUST resolve to an existing schema location and MUST equal the single Event Envelope payload dispatch for that kind. Consumers MUST NOT infer payload schemas from Event.kind spelling, schema-name conventions, or fallback definitions.

For every v1 built-in reducer-input Event kind, plane, sealed, lattice and bottom are frozen registry authority. Realm policy_bundle.cell_lattices is restricted to Realm-specific extension families and MUST NOT shadow, override or reinterpret a built-in cell family.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ak.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.
payload_schema_contract.explicit_binding_rule: Each active standard event kind declares exactly one payload_schema_ref, and the Event Envelope dispatch selects that exact location. Missing, dangling, duplicate, or divergent bindings fail closed. Consumers MUST NOT infer a payload schema from kind spelling or naming conventions.

Authorized event sibling-bucket or full-hash collision resolution. Notary equivocation evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id plus the two conflicting Seal wire objects: same (realm_id, notary_seq) slot with different canonical bytes, or a notary_seq=k+1 Seal that does not descend from the same signer's notary_seq=k Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1). Admission is verification-only: any Realm member MAY submit and the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted and reducer MUST NOT require one. Reducer MUST re-verify both signatures and the slot rule, then add a per-signer fault record to the notary_fault cell. Once a fault record is accepted: receivers MUST reject later Seals signed by the fault signer, the two conflicting Seals and their descendants enter fork_quarantine, and Realm-wide pause applies only when no eligible signer remains.

Notary censorship evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id, the signed control-plane receipt, the seal_ref of the Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the pending Control Move, a control_event_set_root non-membership proof for the censored event digest, and the missing rejection-or-defer proof (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Admission is verification-only: the receipt holder MAY submit; the receipt signature plus the non-membership proof are the complete authorization. This evidence does NOT automatically disqualify the notary: reducer adds an audit fault record that MUST raise governance alarms, feeds inclusion-list / recovery obligations, and is evaluated by governance or the genesis recovery path.

Realm membership state. Agent join/cleanup Events carry an exact agent_controller_binding. Effective Agent membership additionally AND-gates the controller authority pair and bound join Event generation, lifecycle and provision/accountability validity. Controller terminal transitions never synthesize this Event: self leave uses the registered atomic agent_membership_cascade unit; third-party emergency removal freezes a durable exact-set cleanup intent and the original initiator later signs the complete Agent leave set.

Strand business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at; ak.strand.update patch on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on the Strand's discussion track that 'references' this event, and the event log's own actor_id / created_at is the audit source. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=strand_already_terminal; state=archived yields strand_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond these hard invariants.

Unified Strand tracks patch. payload.patch uses ak.schema.patch.v1 against the Strand.tracks map: keys are track names (e.g. `synthesis`, `discussion`), values are patch ops that may toggle enabled, set is_primary, or modify profile / metadata on a track entry. Atomic across multiple tracks.

Strand move between Spaces (target_space_id in payload). Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (board_space_id, strand_id); the contains Relation list_space_id->strand_id is derived from cell value, not a separate truth source. Plane ruling (CBA): v1 freezes ak.component.strand.position.v1 as sealed=true control plane, so ak.strand.move is a Control Move carrying seal_basis. Realm-specific extension declarations cannot override this built-in family.

Strand reorder within Space. Writes the same cell as ak.strand.move; the reducer-projected list_space_id MUST equal head_eq.list_space_id (rank-only update). Plane ruling follows ak.strand.move: v1 freezes the same built-in cell family as sealed=true control plane (models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6), and Realm-specific extension declarations cannot override it.

Set or clear a per-(strand, actor) watch subscription. Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (strand_id, watcher_actor_id). Payload carries level in {mentions_only, participating, all, muted} (or null to clear, equivalent to mentions_only). Default invariant: payload.watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope actor_id, unless writer holds ak.strand.watch.set.others. Cross-actor writes MUST be paired with a same-batch ak.audit.accessed event with access_kind=watch_set_others; the audit event carries refs[role=audit_pair] plus the suite-bearing paired_event_id pointing at the write, and derives its digest from that ID. The write MUST NOT reference the audit event (encoding.md 6.0.1 forbids mutual preimages). The watches Relation (actor --watches--> strand) is a derived projection of this cell, not a separate truth source — direct ak.relation.create relation_kind=watches MUST schema_violation. See models/strand-and-message.md §8.

Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, verification_method, accountable_principal_id, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, and approval_evidence; expires_at is optional (absent means non-expiring, revocation-governed). The agent-key cell is an observed-remove OR-Set. First authorization adds one authorization dot. Same-key re-authorization MUST atomically remove every active authorization dot visible at the Move seal_basis and add the replacement dot; it MUST NOT select a winner by arrival time. Concurrent replacement dots that survive the join are evaluated by the deterministic strictest fold: intersect agent_key_scope and audience, take the earliest finite expires_at (absence is +infinity), and fail closed if accountable_principal_id or verification_method disagree. Key replacement has no dedicated rotate kind: runtime replacement re-pairing authorizes the new key and revokes every prior active key (reason=superseded_by_repairing) in the same accepted transaction.

Agent signing key revocation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_revoke_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, revoked_at, and revoked_by; the revocation's control-plane basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and its cutoff is the accepted Seal covering the Move.

Controller-authored Agent Agent provisioning fact. One Event proof binds the allocated Agent DID, the forward-declared Agent PCR realm id, controller delegation, immutable requested-scope digest, accountability scope and selector. Admission atomically projects the provision, accountability, selector and realm-id-claim cells; no nested payload proof or partial two-Event state is valid. The declared Agent PCR genesis arrives in a later separate submission whose admission reverse-looks-up this declaration.

Controller-owned signed selector statement binding (controller_subject, agent_slug) to one Agent DID. The Event belongs in the controller Principal Control Realm, never the Agent PCR or a Collaboration Realm. Concurrent distinct current values remain visible and make selector resolution ambiguous/fail-closed.

Agent lifecycle transition to paused state. Authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; payload carries no independent frontier. Auth Server MUST reject new agent session grants for this principal; existing tokens fail closed within an independent pause revocation freshness window of at most 60 seconds, never merely the session maximum TTL. Reversible via ak.self.agent.resume.

Agent lifecycle transition from paused to active. Authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; payload carries no independent frontier. At acceptance the reducer MUST use the accepted current control frontier to re-validate controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability_grant freshness; any failure rejects the resume.

Agent lifecycle terminal state. One accepted controller-authorized Event is the unavoidable parent AND gate for every runtime key, session, pairing handle, capability grant, KeyPackage, presence and future submission. Cleanup is asynchronous and MUST NOT synthesize or require child revocation Events. Terminal — no transition out.

Agent-initiated draft proposal. Submitted by agent runtime; Station materializes accepted drafts into controller-owned ak.agent.draft.v1 account-data after capability / policy / accountability / risk check. MUST NOT enter shared Realm history.
Agent-initiated action request. Carries proposed_action, target descriptor, and content digest. Awaits controller approval before generating shared event.

Controller approval of a draft / action request. Binds draft_id, content digest, target descriptor, proposed_action, approved payload digest, approval expiry, and single-use nonce. Publish executor MUST atomic-consume the nonce; reuse fails closed (reason=approval_already_consumed).
Controller rejection of a draft / action request. Draft transitions to rejected; agent runtime MUST NOT continue publish attempts.
Capability Grant genesis. grant.id is omitted; GrantId is derived by retyping this Event's event_id and inserted only in the reducer projection.

Range-bound completeness attestation. Distinct from ak.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event read-your-writes hint) and ak.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity hint): this attestation asserts completeness over an explicit (from_frontier, to_frontier) + per-actor seq interval range. Moderation report. A report authored by the reporter's own device admits as self_authored_proof (actor == subject == payload.reporter). An inbound MIMI report mapped by the provider facade sets payload.provenance=mimi_facade and admits as service_attested: the envelope actor is the facade service DID, payload.reporter carries the Arkret principal resolved under extensions/mimi-interop.md section 11 reporter_authority rules, payload.source_provider_id carries the origin MIMI provider, and the reducer MUST verify the actor service operates the MIMI facade for payload.realm_id. The facade MUST NOT author actor_id as the reporter principal. One accepted Event derives exactly one report and one moderation_queue_item; their full typed IDs differ although both retype the same complete event_id token.

Receiving-service proof that one encrypted target Event was received. The payload is exactly moderation-evidence.schema.json#/$defs/franking_proof; payload.event_id identifies the proven Event and is the ak.component.moderation.franking_proof.v1 cell subject. verification_method selects the exact service key, whose controller must project to received_by and be authorized at received_at. A proof is created independently of any later report, so report_id and target_ref are not payload fields.
Sealed moderation decision (writes ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell)

Submit an appeal against an existing ak.moderation.decision. Writes the appeal cell to state=submitted. appeal_id is omitted and derived by retyping this Event's event_id. Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal strand).
Reviewer acknowledges the appeal and transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Identifies the reviewing actor and target appeal. Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Reviewer's verdict on the appeal: uphold (decision stands) / overturn (decision reversed, emits ak.moderation.decision.lift) / modify (decision adjusted). Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Closes the appeal from submitted / under_review / decided via reviewer close, appellant withdrawal, or a deployment's authorized close service. close is a manual/authorized action; the protocol does not mandate any auto-close timer or cool-off duration (deployment/Realm policy decides). Schema: ak.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

concurrency_class_definitions.merge_safe: Operation commutes under its declared lattice and may execute concurrently with other merge_safe operations after ordinary causal validation.
concurrency_class_definitions.exclusive: Operation requires exclusive compare-and-apply for its target cell set but does not globally serialize unrelated security authority.
concurrency_class_definitions.security_barrier: Authority, membership, key, scope, policy, recovery, or identity transition that serializes against every concurrent security_barrier touching the same signed scope.

merge_definitions.server_revision_cas: Whole-value compare-and-set on expected_revision; accepted revision increments by one and the revision high-water mark survives tombstone GC.
merge_definitions.fsm_cas: Closed FSM transition checked against the family table and current revision; concurrent siblings fail closed.
merge_definitions.cas_register: Single actor-private register; concurrent distinct values fail closed rather than using arrival order.
merge_definitions.causal_then_hlc_then_device: Causal dominance wins; only causally incomparable positions compare HLC, and only equal HLC values compare device_id lexicographically.
